svg.title: Mjölnir — Verification Trust Engine: how it works
svg.desc: Without Mjölnir a pipeline goes tests, pass, looks green. With Mjölnir it goes tests, run, artifacts, evidence, Mjölnir, trust. Mjölnir reads three signals: the test suite and the CI pipeline statically, and the artifacts of a run that already finished — Playwright JSON and JUnit XML — which are the only real run evidence it ingests. It discovers, analyzes, correlates, weighs evidence and measures, across four evidence streams: test quality, CI integrity, runtime forensics and selector health. Every finding is stamped E0 observation, E1 pattern evidence, or E2 deterministic proof, weighted none, half and full; evidence level is earned, not assumed. A trust ladder from L0 to L5 shows the top three rungs require a real run, so static analysis can never claim them. Mjölnir never runs your tests, executes your code, replaces your framework, or proves business correctness. Out come findings such as QA-CI-009, Test command does not propagate exit code, at evidence level E2; an example worthiness score from examples/demo-repo of 75 out of 100 labelled NEEDS WORK, from 27 findings and 4 errors; and a CI gate mapping the frozen exit codes to a trust decision: 0 clean is pass, 1 findings at or above the gate is block, 2 partial scan is investigate, 10 usage error, 20 internal error. That is verification trust, not business correctness. An agent loop runs scan, evidence, handoff, AI agent, re-scan, proof, and the proof returns to Mjölnir for re-verification: AI writes the fix, Mjölnir verifies the fix.

g.text: Mjölnir tells you what you can trust.
A green pipeline is a claim, not a proof.
Evidence level is earned, not assumed.
Static analysis can never claim them.
signals in · evidence out · nothing executed
Test command does not propagate exit code
AI writes the fix. Mjölnir verifies the fix.
Proof comes from the re-scan, never from the agent's report of success.
reads · analyzes · correlates · measures · reports · gates
runs your tests · executes your code · replaces your framework · proves business correctness
Mjölnir scans Mjölnir in its own CI.
A verification trust engine must itself be verifiable.
